data.name: Renoir
data.detailed_description:
James Renoir was a police officer, serving in the main precinct in a metropolis rotten with crime and violence. The influence of the mafia families had even spread through the corridors of city hall like poisonous weeds, all the way to the highest levels of political power. The police, paralyzed by the city’s corrupt government, were powerless to do anything about it – mere toys in the hands of the true power.

However, with a new, young and aspiring politician in city hall, things take a turn for the better and Renoir is promoted to Detective for his effort in the fight against crime. With his new-found access to better classes of society, he eventually meets the woman of his dreams.

But just as everything seems to be heading in the right direction, two shots ring out, turning his world upside-down. Solving this case is now the only thing that matters to him, because as he sits with his back against a cold gravestone, he realizes that the body six feet down is his own...

Now a ghost, Renoir possesses a unique ability that allows him to control phantoms around him and use them to solve environmental puzzles. Seeking justice from the shadows, he must tread carefully and avoid light at all costs. James’s ghostly form must backtrack over his last steps in the world of the living, recollecting his memories and searching for the clues that will lead him back to his murderer.

Features


  • Black and white detective story powered by Unreal Engine 4
  • Puzzle platforming action, inspired by Hollywood noir movies
  • Control phantoms and use them to solve environmental puzzles
  • A murder mystery, narrated through atmospheric comicbook-style movies

data.short_description: Renoir is a story-driven puzzle platformer that draws inspiration from classic 1940s film noir. Detective James Renoir has but a single shot to crack one hell of a case: his own murder!

reviews.review:
Renoir is a stylish supernatural puzzle-platformer that blends classic detective fiction with an unsettling journey through the afterlife. Developed by Black Wing Foundation and published by Fulqrum Publishing, the game places players in the role of James Renoir, a police detective whose promising career ends abruptly when he is murdered. Rather than allowing death to conclude his story, the game transforms his tragic fate into the beginning of a mysterious investigation. Its combination of monochromatic visuals, ghostly abilities, and environmental puzzles creates an intriguing experience that stands apart from conventional platforming adventures. Although its execution occasionally struggles to match its creative ambitions, the unusual premise and distinctive atmosphere provide compelling reasons to explore its shadow-filled world.

The narrative unfolds in a city consumed by organized crime, corruption, and political manipulation. James Renoir initially appears to be an ordinary police officer attempting to maintain justice in a society where criminal organizations possess considerable influence. His dedication eventually leads to professional advancement and opportunities for personal happiness, but these achievements are suddenly destroyed by an unexpected murder. Awakening as a ghost, Renoir discovers that he must uncover the truth behind his death while navigating an existence governed by supernatural restrictions. This premise immediately establishes an engaging mystery, supported by themes of betrayal, ambition, and unfinished business. However, despite its promising foundation, the storytelling sometimes feels more like a backdrop for puzzle solving than a fully developed detective investigation.

Gameplay revolves around navigating two-dimensional environments while manipulating spectral entities to overcome obstacles. Renoir possesses the unusual ability to command other ghosts, allowing him to interact indirectly with objects and mechanisms throughout the environment. These supernatural interactions form the foundation of the puzzle system, requiring players to observe their surroundings, coordinate movements, and determine the appropriate sequence of actions. The puzzles are generally approachable, but certain challenges demand patience and careful planning. Solving a particularly troublesome obstacle can be satisfying, especially when multiple environmental elements must work together. Unfortunately, the limited variety of available interactions gradually becomes noticeable, making some later challenges feel like variations of previously encountered situations.

One of the game's most interesting mechanics involves the protagonist's relationship with light. Because Renoir exists as a ghost, illuminated areas present dangerous barriers that restrict his movement. Players must carefully navigate shadows, manipulate environmental conditions, and use other spirits to create safe passages. This mechanic cleverly connects the supernatural storyline with the actual gameplay, transforming lighting into both an atmospheric feature and a practical obstacle. The resulting challenges encourage strategic thinking rather than reckless movement. Nevertheless, the system occasionally produces frustrating situations where minor mistakes require repeating familiar sequences. The platforming itself is relatively basic, meaning the experience depends more heavily on puzzle design than responsive movement or demanding physical challenges.

The visual presentation is unquestionably among Renoir's strongest qualities. Its black-and-white aesthetic captures the spirit of classic film noir, using dramatic contrasts, deep shadows, and carefully composed environments to create a haunting atmosphere. The monochromatic artwork complements the detective narrative while reinforcing the importance of light and darkness. Cinematic sequences inspired by graphic novels further strengthen the storytelling, presenting important events through stylized imagery. The environments communicate a convincing sense of isolation and mystery, although their limited visual diversity can make certain locations feel repetitive. Even with these shortcomings, the artistic direction gives the adventure a recognizable identity that remains memorable beyond its gameplay mechanics.

Sound design contributes to the mysterious atmosphere through restrained music, environmental effects, and dramatic audio cues. Rather than constantly overwhelming players with intense compositions, the presentation emphasizes tension and uncertainty. The quieter moments are particularly effective because they allow the eerie environments to establish their own mood. Voice acting and cinematic dialogue help communicate the narrative, although the emotional impact varies depending on the scene. Overall, the audiovisual design successfully supports the game's supernatural detective theme, even when the underlying mechanics lack comparable sophistication.

The game's greatest weakness lies in its limited mechanical evolution. While controlling phantoms initially feels creative, the puzzles do not consistently introduce enough fresh ideas to maintain the same level of excitement throughout the adventure. Some sequences depend on repetition rather than discovery, and the relatively rigid solutions leave little opportunity for experimentation. The linear structure also limits replayability, since completing the mystery and understanding the puzzle solutions removes much of the incentive to return. Nine Steam achievements and trading card support provide minor additional incentives, but the experience remains focused on a single narrative journey rather than extensive long-term engagement.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially classified as Unknown, meaning Valve has not confirmed whether the game meets its handheld compatibility standards. Its modest Windows system requirements suggest that demanding hardware performance is unlikely to be the main concern, but Proton compatibility, controller functionality, and display readability remain unverified. Players interested in experiencing the adventure on Steam Deck should therefore anticipate possible configuration adjustments rather than assuming seamless operation.

Ultimately, Renoir is an imaginative but imperfect adventure that succeeds most convincingly through its atmospheric presentation and unusual supernatural premise. Its striking visual style, mysterious storyline, and ghost-manipulation mechanics offer a worthwhile experience for enthusiasts of noir-inspired puzzle games. However, repetitive challenges, limited gameplay variety, and underdeveloped investigative elements prevent it from achieving its full potential. It is best recommended to players who value artistic atmosphere and intriguing concepts over sophisticated mechanics or extensive replayability. Despite its shortcomings, the adventure possesses enough personality to remain an interesting example of experimental independent game design.

A visually memorable supernatural detective adventure with clever environmental ideas and a captivating noir atmosphere, weakened by repetitive puzzles and limited gameplay depth.

Rating: 6/10
